responsibility: This module is the GCC Rust frontend’s backend lowering and code-generation bridge, responsible for turning resolved Rust HIR and TyTy semantic types into GCC tree IR, declarations, and emitted symbols. Its main compile-* families divide that job across crate/item orchestration, type translation, expression/statement/block lowering, parameter and pattern handling, path and impl/extern resolution, inline assembly, struct construction, and special handling for intrinsics, constexpr/const evaluation, and procedural macro crate metadata. Supporting infrastructure here includes the central compilation context that caches compiled types, functions, variables, and monomorphized instances, the builtin and intrinsic registries that map Rust operations onto GCC builtins or synthetic functions, symbol mangling for Rust ABI names, and Rust-specific tree utilities and coercion logic for references, unsizing, trait objects, and constant folding. In short, this module owns the Rust-specific backend semantics needed to convert analyzed Rust programs into GCC’s generic IR and backend-facing global/function/type representations.
